## The question

College volleyball players vary in height, position, and playing style. This project asks whether taller players also have stronger on-court statistics, or whether height alone is a poor measure of performance.

> **Research question:** Is player height associated with better college volleyball statistics after accounting for differences between positions?

## Study map

The central comparison is height and performance, while position and playing context help explain the relationship.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
	H[Player height] --> P[Performance statistics]
	S[Playing position] --> P
	S --> H
	T[Training and team strategy] --> P
	M[Matches and playing time] --> P
	P --> K[Kills and hitting]
	P --> B[Blocks]
	P --> D[Digs and aces]

	classDef focus fill:#0f766e,color:#ffffff,stroke:#115e59,stroke-width:2px;
	classDef context fill:#fef3c7,color:#78350f,stroke:#d97706;
	class H,P focus;
	class S,T,M context;
```

## Height signal explorer

Try a position and height to see how the expected statistical profile shifts. This is an **illustrative interaction**, not a result from the project dataset.

```{=html}
<section class="evidence-lab" aria-label="Interactive height signal explorer">

	<p class="lab-kicker">Interactive evidence lab</p>
	<h2 class="lab-heading">Change the player. Watch the profile move.</h2>
	<p class="lab-description">The same height can mean something different depending on a player's role. Use the controls to explore that idea before the real data are analyzed.</p>
	<div class="lab-grid">
		<div class="lab-controls">
			<span class="lab-label">Choose a position</span>
			<div class="position-buttons" role="group" aria-label="Choose a volleyball position">
				<button class="active" data-position="Middle blocker">Middle blocker</button>
				<button data-position="Outside hitter">Outside hitter</button>
				<button data-position="Libero">Libero</button>
				<button data-position="Setter">Setter</button>
			</div>
			<label class="lab-label" for="height-range">Player height</label>
			<div class="height-readout"><span class="height-value" id="height-value">74 in</span><span id="height-cm">188 cm</span></div>
			<input class="height-range" id="height-range" type="range" min="60" max="82" value="74" aria-label="Player height in inches">
			<div class="range-notes"><span>5'0"</span><span>6'10"</span></div>
		</div>
		<div class="lab-output" aria-live="polite">
			<div class="output-header"><span class="lab-label">Illustrative profile</span><span class="output-position" id="output-position">Middle blocker</span></div>
			<p class="output-note" id="output-note">Height may show its clearest signal in net play.</p>
			<div class="stat-row"><span class="stat-name">Kills</span><span class="stat-track"><span class="stat-fill" id="kills-fill"></span></span><span class="stat-score" id="kills-score"></span></div>
			<div class="stat-row"><span class="stat-name">Blocks</span><span class="stat-track"><span class="stat-fill" id="blocks-fill"></span></span><span class="stat-score" id="blocks-score"></span></div>
			<div class="stat-row"><span class="stat-name">Digs</span><span class="stat-track"><span class="stat-fill" id="digs-fill"></span></span><span class="stat-score" id="digs-score"></span></div>
			<div class="stat-row"><span class="stat-name">Aces</span><span class="stat-track"><span class="stat-fill" id="aces-fill"></span></span><span class="stat-score" id="aces-score"></span></div>
		</div>
	</div>
	<p class="lab-footnote">The bars are a visual model for thinking about the question. They are not observed college volleyball statistics.</p>

</section>

<script>
const positionProfiles = {
	"Middle blocker": { note: "Height may show its clearest signal in net play.", base: [58, 82, 18, 28], weight: [0.7, 1.2, 0.1, 0.2] },
	"Outside hitter": { note: "A broad role makes context and playing time especially important.", base: [68, 48, 42, 36], weight: [0.8, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3] },
	"Libero": { note: "Defensive impact is a useful test of whether height is overstated.", base: [12, 8, 86, 35], weight: [0.1, 0.05, -0.5, 0.2] },
	"Setter": { note: "Decision-making and team system may matter more than reach.", base: [34, 22, 38, 48], weight: [0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.5] }
};

const heightRange = document.querySelector("#height-range");
const heightValue = document.querySelector("#height-value");
const heightCm = document.querySelector("#height-cm");
const outputPosition = document.querySelector("#output-position");
const outputNote = document.querySelector("#output-note");
const statNames = ["kills", "blocks", "digs", "aces"];
let selectedPosition = "Middle blocker";

function updateExplorer() {
	const height = Number(heightRange.value);
	const profile = positionProfiles[selectedPosition];
	const differenceFromAverage = height - 71;
	heightValue.textContent = `${Math.floor(height / 12)}'${height % 12}"`;
	heightCm.textContent = `${Math.round(height * 2.54)} cm`;
	outputPosition.textContent = selectedPosition;
	outputNote.textContent = profile.note;
	profile.base.forEach((value, index) => {
		const score = Math.max(5, Math.min(98, Math.round(value + differenceFromAverage * profile.weight[index])));
		document.querySelector(`#${statNames[index]}-fill`).style.width = `${score}%`;
		document.querySelector(`#${statNames[index]}-score`).textContent = `${score}`;
	});
}

document.querySelectorAll(".position-buttons button").forEach((button) => {
	button.addEventListener("click", () => {
		document.querySelectorAll(".position-buttons button").forEach((item) => item.classList.remove("active"));
		button.classList.add("active");
		selectedPosition = button.dataset.position;
		updateExplorer();
	});
});

heightRange.addEventListener("input", updateExplorer);
updateExplorer();
</script>
```

## What will be compared

The analysis will compare height with performance measures such as:

- kills and kills per set
- hitting percentage
- blocks and blocks per set
- digs and digs per set
- service aces

Position matters because a middle blocker and a libero are expected to contribute in different ways. The analysis should therefore look at the overall relationship and then examine positions separately.

## Working hypothesis

Height may be most strongly related to blocking and attacking statistics. However, a relationship between height and a statistic would not show that height causes better performance. Skill, training, playing time, team strategy, and position may also explain differences between players.

## Analysis plan

1. Clean the player-level data and check for missing values.
2. Summarize height and statistics with tables and visualizations.
3. Use scatterplots and correlations to examine relationships.
4. Compare results across playing positions.
5. Fit regression models that include height and position together.

The conclusion will focus on the strength and uncertainty of the evidence, not on whether height is a universal requirement for success.

## Current status

This page now includes an official NCAA 2025-season benchmark. The next step is to combine player heights, positions, and individual statistics so the project can test whether height is associated with performance within and across positions.
